test.name: 'Write this up' on a project with a proof summary produces a report from project state alone
test.description: The researcher asks for a written report. The main thread builds it from tool reads (project_context, research_query on proof_summaries, conflicts, evaluations and plans, tree_query), spawns no agent, never calls research_append, never reads research.json or tree.gedcomx.json directly, and ends on no 'Continue with' line. The report carries the tier in words, the reviewer's verdict, the resolved conflict and what was not yet searched. Issue #4576.

input.user_message: Write this up for me so I can keep it.

negative.explanation: A written report is a bounded deliverable the main thread writes itself, like a records-request letter (MCP App plan M2). The validator gates: research_query on proof_summaries and evaluations; no agent spawn; no research_append; no direct read of the raw project files; the report text (reply plus any Write content or Bash command) names the tier 'probable', the reviewer's verdict (looks solid), the resolved birthplace conflict, and the 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses as not yet searched.

judge_context: The report must come from project state and add no claim: every fact in it must be in this scenario. The deterministic validator cannot check that; the judge does.

Facts of this scenario: the question is who the parents of Patrick Flynn (b. about 1845, PA, d. 1908) were. The proof summary rates it probable: Patrick is probably the son of Thomas Flynn of Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, from the 1850 and 1860 censuses and the 1908 death certificate. One conflict, Patrick's birthplace (Ireland in the 1850 and 1860 censuses, Pennsylvania on the 1908 death certificate), is resolved in favour of Ireland because the censuses are contemporary and the death certificate's informant, a son-in-law, is secondary. The search summary lists the 1850 census on FamilySearch, Ancestry and MyHeritage, the 1860 census and the death certificate; probate is in progress; the 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses are not yet searched.
The reviewer's verdict is 'looks solid', from an on-demand review of the parentage question. A report that calls it anything stronger, or presents any other read as the reviewer's verdict, fails.
A report that states a fact not above (a birth date for Thomas, a spouse, a record not named) fails the no-new-claims dimension.
The reply must not end on a 'Continue with ...?' line.
